ruling.recommended_action: Refund the excess distance fare for the non-exempt 2.88 km, issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (no formal warning — first notification incident)
ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation with an agreed-but-qualified reroute. The optimal route was 8.4 km; the actual route was 11.6 km, a deviation of +3.2 km [F1], well over the 1 km tolerance in RD-1, so a refund is in scope. The code isolated one off-route segment, 12:11–12:17, +2.88 km, driving Faber Drive → Jalan Lempeng → Clementi Ave 6 → Commonwealth Ave West → Clementi Avenue 4 → Clementi Ave 5 → Clementi Ave 2 → West Coast Road → Jalan Mas Kuning [F3].

Traffic: Ayer Rajah Expressway was in speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 11:58 to 12:17, i.e. active before the segment began and throughout it [F11], and no incidents were recorded [F14]. The driver's 12:07 message warned of that congestion and asked whether to take another way [F7], and the rider replied at 12:08, before the segment started: “Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4” [F8, F9]. Notice was therefore timely [F7], but the consent was qualified.

Under RD-5 the code checks the named road against the roads actually driven: the segment drove Clementi Avenue 4 [F3], the very road the rider excluded. A qualified yes (“ok, but not via Y”) does not cover a segment that drove Y, and a traffic reason (RD-4) cannot enlarge the rider's consent where the rider has narrowed it. RD-3 also does not exempt the segment, because the rider's agreement was to avoid Clementi Avenue 4, not to take it. The driver's post-trip statement that “the rider said can” [F10] is a claim that omits the qualification in the timestamped chat [F8] and cannot override the written record. Accordingly the +2.88 km counts as a deviation.

Refund: the whole-trip excess distance fare is $4.50 for 3.19 km at $1.4096/km [F4] — the trip's own per-km distance fare, as RD-2 requires. The single identified segment of 2.88 km is the bulk of that excess; the residual ~0.31 km is map-matching-scale leave from the 0.32 km exempt portion (traffic reason under RD-4) and is not refunded either way. Refund = 2.88 km × $1.4096/km = $4.06. Tolls, time fare and any surge are not refunded (RD-2); surge was 1.0×, so no surge element [F5], and the rest of the $26.08 build-up stands [F6].

Driver side: this is not a repeat route deviation — the profile's single upheld dispute is a no-show matter (route upheld: 0) [F17], so RD-6's flag_account does not apply. RD-7 does apply: the driver did tell the rider, but did not honour the rider's qualification, so send a notification-duty reminder and log it on his route-compliance record; no formal warning as a first such incident.

Amount is under $10 and the record is complete (GPS segment, timestamped chat, fare breakdown, traffic data), so this is decided at system level (TH-1, TH-2, C1; cf. PREC-1/DISP-2026-0089 — uninformed/unconsented reroute, excess distance fare refunded). No safety content appears in the chat, complaint or driver statement: the messages concern route choice only.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 12:08 reply is a qualified yes — "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4" — and the driver's notice at 12:07 preceded the segment (12:11–12:17), so consent to reroute existed. But the qualified consent does not cover a route that drives Clementi Avenue 4 [F3]; the segment drove it, so RD-5's named-road check fails (named_road_untied) and the +2.88 km is not exempt. RD-4 is met in form (Ayer Rajah Expressway, speed band 2, active 11:58–12:17 [F11]), but under RD-2/RD-5 a traffic reason cannot enlarge the rider's consent: the rider's own instructions define the agreed route.

The remaining 0.32 km is treated as exempt: congestion on the replaced part of the recommended route (Ayer Rajah Expressway, band 2, under 19 km/h, active before and throughout the segment, within tolerance band of the route) gives a traffic reason under RD-4, and 0.32 km is only map-matching-scale leave [F1, F3].

element_findings.reason: Multiplier at trip start was 1.0× [F5], identical to the quote, so no surge notice was required and SURGE-1/SURGE-2 do not apply.

element_findings.element: Driver's stated reason for the reroute (RD-4/RD-5)
element_findings.reason: The driver's chat message at 12:07 stated a reason and asked before the segment began at 12:11 [F7, F3], so notice existed; however the traffic explanation only addresses whether a reroute was justified, not whether the rider's qualification (not via Clementi Avenue 4) was respected. His post-trip statement that the rider 'said can' without noting the qualification [F10] is his claim and cannot override the timestamped rider chat [F8, F9].

The driver's profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld, but that upheld dispute is a no-show matter (route upheld = 0) [F17]; RD-6 requires an upheld route deviation in the last 90 days, so no account flag is warranted.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider simply 'said can' omits the explicit limitation in the rider's own timestamped message ('but not via Clementi Avenue 4') [F8, F9]; under A7/RD-5 a claim of blanket agreement cannot override the written record.

The driver's traffic warning, while truthful as to Ayer Rajah Expressway congestion [F11], does not convert the rider's qualified consent into agreement to drive Clementi Avenue 4; a traffic reason never exempts a segment the rider expressly excluded (RD-5).
